hero.eyebrow: Stripe reports, one for each reader
hero.title: Stop building the Monday report.
hero.lead: Monday, 9am. The board wants one page. Support wants the failed payments. Your CFO wants retention. Today someone builds all three by hand. SaasReport builds each one from your Stripe data, in the order that reader cares about, and sends it on a schedule.
hero.note: Pre-launch. Be one of the first companies we build this for.

problem.title: The same month. Ten different questions.

items.title: Monday, 9am
items.text: The board wants one page. Support wants the failed payments. The CFO wants retention. Someone opens Stripe and starts three exports.

items.title: The sheet nobody trusts
items.text: Numbers get pasted, filtered and renamed on the way. Two people pull the same month and get two answers.

items.title: One view for everyone
items.text: The Stripe Dashboard is built for the person who runs Stripe. Everyone else asks that person for a screenshot.

how.title: One set of numbers. One report per reader.
how.lead: SaasReport reads your Stripe data and computes every figure by the same written rules. Then it builds each reader's report and sends it.

steps.title: Install the app in Stripe.
steps.text: SaasReport asks for read access only. It never moves money and never changes your account.

steps.title: Pick who gets what.
steps.text: Choose a reader, a report and a schedule. Each report says which schedules it supports.

steps.title: Code computes every number.
steps.text: Each figure follows a published definition. Rules turn the figures into findings, with the evidence beside them. AI words the summary and never writes a figure.

steps.title: Each reader gets a link.
steps.text: The email names the report and carries no figures. The link is signed, it expires, and you can revoke it.
steps.example: The report is a PDF stored under your own tenant.

how.status: We have written down the {stakeholders} readers, {metrics} metrics and {reports} report types, and built the engine that computes the numbers. The Stripe app, the report pages and the email are next. The examples on this page run that engine on sample data.

people.title: Pick who is asking.
people.lead: A CEO, a CFO, a board member, a support lead: each asks something different of the same month. Choose one. See their questions, the figures they follow, what reaches them, and what Stripe cannot tell them.
people.sampleNote: The figures are computed by the real engine on made-up sample data for the last complete month.

who.title: Who asks

who.noFindingLine: No finding fires for them on this sample month.

order.title: Same data. The order follows the reader.

order.summary: Open the same report as three different readers.

findings.title: Every finding names its evidence.

sectors.title: If you take payments through Stripe, one of these is you.

items.title: Subscription businesses
items.text: Recurring revenue, retention and churn for the CEO, CFO, board and investors, plus new customers for sales and marketing. Reports: {reports}. Needs Stripe Billing subscriptions.

items.title: Merchants without subscriptions
items.text: Payments, refunds and disputes for finance and support. Reports: {reports}. They read charges, refunds and disputes only, so no subscriptions are needed.

items.title: Marketplaces and platforms
items.text: What the platform earns, and how its refunds and disputes behave. Report: {reports}. Stripe lets an app on a platform read only the platform's own data. Your merchants install SaasReport on their own accounts, and you can recommend it. That is a referral, not a data feed.

sectors.platformNote: Stripe lets an app installed by a platform read only the platform's own data.

delivery.eyebrow: How a report reaches a person
delivery.title: A signed link, not an attachment.
delivery.lead: Each report is stored as a PDF under your own tenant. The reader gets an email with a link. It is signed and it expires. The email shows no figures, and you can revoke the link.
delivery.why: A financial report is sensitive. An attachment is copied, forwarded and kept for ever. A link can expire, can be revoked, and shows when it was opened.

journey.title: From Stripe data to a signed link
journey.summary: The path of one report. Every stage is planned.

steps.title: Stripe sends the data
steps.text: Charges, refunds, disputes and subscriptions arrive through the Stripe app, and are stored under your tenant only.

steps.title: Code computes the figures
steps.text: A deterministic engine turns the data into integers under published definitions.

steps.title: Rules write the findings
steps.text: Published rules read the figures and state what changed, with the evidence.

steps.title: AI words the summary
steps.text: The AI sees aggregates only. A number guard rejects any number the engine did not compute.

steps.title: The PDF is stored
steps.text: The report is saved under your tenant's own prefix.

steps.title: A signed link is emailed
steps.text: The reader gets a link that expires. The email carries no figures.

schedule.title: Which period each schedule covers
schedule.text: A scheduled run reports on the last complete period, in UTC. This is what each cadence would cover on the date this page was built.
schedule.summary: The five cadences and the period each one covers.

trust.title: What we promise, and where each promise stands.
trust.lead: These are written commitments. Each has a status, read from our commitments register. A commitment moves from planned to implemented only when a test or a file proves it. Today they are all planned, because the product is not built yet.

legal.label: Legal documents
legal.text: {count} documents are drafts and none is published: {titles}. Company facts they need are not set yet: {missing}.

access.title: Who sees which report
access.text: A person sees a report only if their Stripe role already lets them see the data behind it. A role we do not know sees nothing.
access.summary: Pick a group of Stripe roles to see which reports they could read.
access.heldLabel: Held back, because their role cannot see the data
access.noneLabel: No report: this role cannot see financial data.
access.step: A person opens SaasReport. We read their Stripe roles and offer only the reports those roles can see.

guard.title: AI writes the words. Code owns the numbers.
guard.text: Every figure comes from the engine. A guard checks each sentence the AI drafts, and rejects it if it holds a number the engine did not compute. A rejected sentence is never repaired.
guard.summary: Run two drafted sentences through the guard.

stages.detail: Each number must be one the engine computed.

cases.label: A sentence with the engine's number
cases.draft: Net revenue retention came in at {nrr}, a little under full retention.

cases.label: A sentence with an invented number
cases.draft: Net revenue retention came in at 112.40%, well ahead of plan.

items.a: Not yet. The engine that computes the numbers is built and tested. The Stripe app, the report pages and the email delivery are not. Ask for early access and we will tell you when we start building for you.

Nothing is stored yet, because nothing is built. The design is: read-only access, data kept under your own tenant identifier, encryption in transit, and no use of your data to train AI. Each promise is a commitment in the register above with its status.
A person sees a report only if their Stripe role already lets them see the data behind it. A role we do not know sees nothing. Try it in the Trust section.

It cannot. Code computes every figure. The AI is meant to write only the sentences around them, and a guard rejects any sentence that holds a number the engine did not compute. The guard exists in code. Try it in the Trust section.
Only what the reports need: {classes}. It reads nothing today.
We have not set prices. Early-access companies help us decide what is fair.
There is no date. We will not invent one. Early access is how we choose what to build first.

items.q: What can it not tell me?
items.a: Anything Stripe does not hold. Across the readers above that includes {gaps}. SaasReport will not pretend to know them.

items.q: I run a marketplace. Can I see my merchants' numbers?
items.a: Not through SaasReport. Stripe lets an app installed by a platform read only the platform's own data. Merchants can install SaasReport on their own accounts, and you can recommend it.

items.q: Is it in the Stripe App Marketplace?
items.a: No. It is not listed there.
SaasReport. The legal entity is not set up on paper yet: {company}.

useCases.reports: Build the report for the reader

page.title: Examples
page.intro: Every widget here runs the real SaasReport engine on made-up sample data, or on your own inputs. Each one says which.
page.metaDescription: Interactive examples of SaasReport: pick a reader, see a report ordered for them, count the cost of hand-built reports, and follow a report from Stripe data to a signed link. Sample data only.

who-asks.how: Pick a reader in the People section, and again in the gallery of examples.
who-asks.application: The reader reports of the SaasReport app
who-asks.flow: The registry names the reader, the engine computes the priority figures from sample data, and the rules state the findings.
who-asks.learns: What each reader asks, which figures they follow, and what Stripe cannot tell them.
who-asks.does: Pick a reader and read their questions, figures and findings.

report-order.how: Shown in the People section, below the reader picker.
report-order.application: The report planner of the SaasReport app
report-order.flow: The planner orders the sections of one report type by the reader's priority figures, and the engine fills in each figure.
report-order.learns: That one report type is ordered differently for each of its readers.
report-order.does: Open the same report as three readers and compare the order.

findings.how: Shown in the People section, after the report order.
findings.application: The findings of the SaasReport reports
findings.flow: The engine computes the figures for this month and the month before, and each published rule that matches becomes a finding with its evidence.
findings.learns: That a finding is a written rule with evidence, and what to look at next.
findings.does: Read each finding and the figures behind it.

cost.application: A calculator on the landing page
cost.flow: Your four inputs go through three sums: hours, cost each month and cost each year. Nothing leaves your browser.
cost.learns: What hand-built reporting costs you today, with no claim about savings.
cost.does: Change the four inputs and watch the three results.

roles-access.application: Role-based access in the SaasReport app
roles-access.flow: A report is offered only if every data class behind its figures is visible to at least one of the person's Stripe roles.
roles-access.learns: That access follows Stripe roles, and an unknown role sees nothing.
roles-access.does: Pick a group of Stripe roles and see the reports it could read.

journey.application: The report pipeline of the SaasReport app
journey.flow: Stripe data is stored per tenant, turned into figures and findings, worded, rendered to a PDF, stored, and sent as a signed link.
journey.learns: The path one report takes from Stripe data to a reader, and that every stage is still planned.
journey.does: Run the pipeline and read each stage.

schedule.how: Shown in the Delivery section, after the pipeline.
schedule.application: The schedule of the SaasReport app
schedule.flow: Each cadence reports on the last complete period before the run, in UTC, by integer calendar arithmetic.
schedule.does: Read the five cadences and their periods.

number-guard.how: Shown in the Trust section, after the access example.
number-guard.application: The number guard of the SaasReport reports
number-guard.flow: The guard compares every number in a drafted sentence with the figures the engine computed, and rejects the sentence on any other number.
number-guard.learns: That AI writes the words and code owns the numbers.
number-guard.does: Run a grounded sentence and an invented one through the guard.
